item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; Arkansas Razorbacks running back Cam Settles (27) carries against the Auburn Tigers during the first quarter at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor The Razorbacks had the lead, explosive runs, and a late answer on offense. They still could not contain Byrum Brown or finish a game they had every opportunity to win. Arkansas does not need a participation trophy for making a loss more competitive. The Razorbacks needed a victory. They built an early lead, carried an advantage into the fourth quarter, and delivered a late touchdown to tie the game. Then Auburn drove into field-goal range and won 26-23 on Alex McPherson’s 43-yard kick with 33 seconds remaining. Razorback Report Card: Auburn Postgame Arkansas fell to 3-6 overall and 1-5 in SEC play. Yes, this was better than Missouri. That is a remarkably low bar for a program asking supporters to remain invested in its direction. The pregame report card established the expectations before kickoff. Contain Brown. Establish the running game. Protect possessions. Finish opportunities. Those standards do not become unreasonable because Arkansas failed to meet them. Run Defense: F The assignment was not a secret. Keep Brown from becoming Auburn’s most dependable rushing threat. Maintain responsibilities when he leaves the pocket. Make the Tigers find another answer. The pregame benchmark required Arkansas to hold Brown below 60 rushing yards and prevent a quarterback run of 20 yards or more. He finished with 120 yards, including a 39-yard fourth-quarter run. That is not narrowly missing the target. That lets the specific problem identified before kickoff become a central reason for losing. Brown gained 125 rushing yards after halftime, overcoming his negative first-half total. His five-yard touchdown run gave Auburn its first lead. His later rushing contributions helped the Tigers produce their final touchdown and winning field-goal drive. Arkansas deserves credit for containing him early. It can’t hide behind that first half after he took control of the second. A defensive plan is not successful simply because it worked before the opponent adjusted. Responding to that adjustment is part of the job. Pass Defense: D The passing yardage was manageable. The moments were not. Brown threw two touchdown passes after halftime and completed 10 of 14 second-half attempts. item.title: UCF football gets late heroics from Alonza Barnett III in wild win over Kansas
item.description: UCF threw away a three-score, second-half lead on the road for the second time in just over a month. Only this time, Alonza Barnett III — the redshirt senior brought in from James Madison to lead the Knights back to prominence — delivered a signature, final-minute drive for the win. Barnett hit tight end Caden Piening for a 6-yard touchdown pass with one second remaining, and Will Stone knocked through the decisive PAT in a 33-32 rally past Kansas on Nov. 7 at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium. The Knights improved to 5-4 overall and 3-3 in the Big 12, moving to within one win of bowl eligibility with three games left. More importantly, Scott Frost and his players finally silenced the conversation of UCF's woes on the road. The 12-game skid, dating back to September 2024, is dead. Asked if he could describe his emotions after watching the Knights surrender a 26-7 lead and complete a final comeback, Frost said, "I could try to describe it, but it would come up short." "We've been involved in two pretty special games, as good of college football games as I've been involved (with) in a long time," Frost added, referring to UCF's double-overtime win over BYU on Oct. 24. "I thought it was two evenly matched teams and just the way the game went was really strange to me. I feel blessed that we were able to go down and get the play at the end of the game." Here are three takeaways from another dramatic Big 12 battle. Alonza Barnett III rewards UCF's faith with clutch drive Saturday's final drive was exactly what Frost and his staff envisioned when pursuing Barnett in the transfer portal, and exactly what Knights fans hoped to see in an experienced, accomplished quarterback. Barnett suffered a hamstring injury on the final drive of UCF's 12-7 loss at Pittsburgh on Sept. 12. He missed the next five games, only returning to action in a backup role last week in a blowout defeat to Baylor . Concerns for Barnett's mobility were put to rest in the first half as he scrambled away from pressure and picked up several nice gains on designed run plays. And he provided an element in the vertical passing game that was noticeably absent for two months, connecting on a 44-yard strike to Josh Derry that gave UCF a 26-7 lead little more than five minutes into the second half. "I (saw) a dawg, somebody that was hungry to come out there and prove himself, especially missing so many games," Derry said. Kansas stymied UCF on three straight drives as the defensive line trio of Blake Herold, Leroy Harris III and David Santiago imposed its will. They were responsible for 9½ of the Jayhawks' 11 tackles for loss on the day, including Harris' three sacks. That coincided with Kansas catching fire and scoring 25 unanswered points, reclaiming the lead with 1:06 to play on Dylan Edwards' 2-yard hurdle into the end zone. item.title: One daring shot was all La Salle needed to repeat as state soccer champs
item.description: PROVIDENCE – Camryn Bromage just couldn't help herself, and that turned out to be the best thing for La Salle on this Saturday afternoon at Rhode Island College. The junior midfielder had time to take a shot midway through the first half against Cumberland. That it was from all of 35 yards, or that coach Stephanie Goulet would have preferred a pass elsewhere, will ultimately just become details in a story they'll remember for years to come. Bromage managed to find the net and make the difference at Alumni Stadium as the Rams sealed back-to-back Division I titles with a 1-0 win over the Clippers under gray skies on Nov. 7. "My coach was like, 'Do not take that shot.' It was a little far out," Bromage said. "But I had the space, I had the opportunity and I just shot it." Watch RI high school sports on NFHS! Bromage took aim in the 15th minute after a tense start between a pair of familiar contenders. Her right-footed effort skipped at the top of the 6-yard box and found its way inside the right post, aided by turf still slick from the overnight rain. That moment allowed La Salle to flip what was its lone defeat of the season, a loss by the same score line against Cumberland at home. "It's a wet game," Bromage said. "The field is slippery. It just so happened it went through." The Rams kept a 12th clean sheet of the season to bring this one home, with central defender Jill Handrahan claiming tournament Most Valuable Player honors. Grace Keenan was forced to make just two saves, and one of those came off a corner kick when Shea Maher tried to force one home with her chest in the 54th minute. "I know a lot of the girls on their team," Handrahan said. "I know how good they are. Going into it I was a little nervous." The Clippers nearly opened the scoring in the first minute. Paynter Maher's cross off the right wing flashed across an open net, but Milana Izzo couldn't get a touch on it to put it away. Cumberland didn't force a save from Keenan before the break, with La Salle gradually taking control of the play as the half progressed. "I feel like we brought the energy," Handrahan said. "Everybody was just working so hard." The Rams (14-1-3) and Clippers (15-2-2) exploded for a combined 12 goals while dispatching North Kingstown and Mt. Hope, respectively, in the semifinals. This was a different sort of 80 minutes in the title round, and La Salle joined the Skippers among programs to finish off recent repeat titles at the top level. North Kingstown beat the Rams in 2021 and 2022 before La Salle returned the favor in 2025. "It's hard to win it two times in a row," Bromage said. "I'm just so happy we were able to accomplish that for our seniors and for everybody." CUMBERLAND (0): No scoring. LA SALLE (1): Camryn Bromage; assist – Lila Slagle. Halftime – LS, 1-0. item.title: Norfolk State’s Michael Vick gives explanation for failed victory formation in 29-28 loss
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Norfolk State’s Michael Vick gives explanation for failed victory formation in 29-28 loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It looked like Michael Vick and his Norfolk State Spartans were closing in on a huge in-conference win against a surging North Carolina Central Eagles team , but the unthinkable happened with 1:34 left. North Carolina Central had no timeouts, and Norfolk State had the ball and could have run out the clock to secure the victory. But instead, the Spartans ran another play and ultimately fumbled, leading North Carolina Central to recover and ultimately score a touchdown to surge ahead 29-28. Michael Vick on the crucial fumble that opened the door for Norfolk State's stunning defeat to North Carolina Central. @WTKR3 pic.twitter.com/rJBWUCF9Dx — Marc Davis (@marcdavissports) November 7, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In postgame comments, Vick tried to explain what happened. “I don’t know what happened at the end of the game. I put my headset down, I called victory formation. All we had to do was just take a knee and nail the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out, and they had, I think, zero timeouts left, and the game was over practically.” When a reporter asked him to clarify, Vick repeated that he called victory and said he doesn’t know why a run play was called. “I put my headset down, and I took my headset off ’cause all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out. I just called victory. I don’t know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don’t know what happened. I really don’t. I don’t know what the play call was. I don’t know why we even ran that play.” Vick said the play will be used as a teaching example across the country and stressed once more that he called victory formation. “People will look at that and that’ll go on as a teaching tape for a lot of teams across the country for years to come. I hate it had to be us, but I called victory formation. I’m just letting everybody know that.” Related: North Carolina Central narrowly beat Michael Vick, Norfolk State 29-28 Related: The anatomy of an upset: Fort Valley State beats Florida A&M in early season action

item.title: Is Jeremiah Smith’s Ohio State career over? Damien Harris makes the case
item.description: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Is Jeremiah Smith’s Ohio State career over? Damien Harris makes the case appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ohio State football saw a different side of Jeremiah Smith Saturday during the 41-28 Oregon rout . And that scene could very well spark the final days of the junior Buckeyes wideout, per Damien Harris. The former New England Patriots running back turned CBS Sports analyst weighed in on Smith’s Columbus future. And Harris’s words will turn heads and grab eyeballs. “He’s done, he’s going to pack it up. In my opinion, there’s nothing to gain, there’s everything to lose if you’re Jeremiah Smith. I don’t think that he plays again the rest of the season for Ohio State,” Harris proclaimed. “What’s there to play for? This isn’t a College Football Playoff team. They were already on the outside looking in. He’s already etched his name in history and he has a national championship. But what’s there to play for?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "In my opinion, there's nothing to gain, there's everything to lose if you're Jeremiah Smith. I don't think that he plays again the rest of the season for Ohio State." 👀 @DHx34 #CFBPostgame pic.twitter.com/ezHkYeUx7D — CBS Sports College Football 🏈 (@CBSSportsCFB) November 8, 2026 Harris insists that he’s not knocking OSU, coach Ryan Day , or even quarterback Luke Fahey who needed to step in for the injured Julian Sayin against Indiana . He also adds that if there’s any game that Smith would entertain playing in, it’s the annual rivalry game versus Michigan. Which takes place after Thanksgiving on Nov. 28 in Columbus. That could very well be Smith’s last game inside the Horseshoe amid his NFL Draft chatter. Smith continues to garner top pick hype especially before facing the Ducks. He still surpassed 100 yards receiving and shattered Marvin Harrison Jr.’s previous mark in the process . But now he and the Buckeyes have endured their most losses together with three defeats. Hence why Harris believes it’s time to shut down Smith if you’re Day and OSU. item.title: “Amazing What Women Are Willing to Do To Each Other”: 5x WNBA All-Star Draws Backlash After What She Said About Sophie Cunningham
item.description: Sophie Cunningham ©Credits: IMAGO “In the women’s game, is it really about how good you are or the visibility, how pretty you are?” Angel McCoughtry has set off a big debate with this one question. The five-time WNBA All-Star said on the Get to the Point podcast that looks and visibility can matter more than talent when it comes to endorsements, and she used Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham as her example. When the hosts asked if she thought Caitlin Clark was pretty, McCoughtry laughed and moved on without answering. The clip drew a fast response from analysts on Fox News’ The Big Weekend Show , and one host said what bothered her most. “It’s amazing to me how the WNBA and the players in the WNBA, their league is getting attention that helps and benefits all of them, but you see certain players actively badmouthing the ones who are bringing the attention, the money, and the eyeballs to their league. And it’s just amazing to me what women are willing to do to each other at their own detriment,” she said. Tensions are boiling over in the WNBA. item.title: Elmira, Horseheads fall in NYSPHSAA girls soccer regional finals
item.description: A pair of Section 4 girls soccer champions from Chemung County saw their seasons come to a close Saturday, Nov. 7 at Chenango Valley High School. Elmira lost by a 1-0 score to Section 1's Arlington in a New York State Public High School Athletic Association Class AAA regional final/state quarterfinal. Horseheads came up short, 3-1, against Section 11's Northport in a Class AA regional final that followed. The lone Section 4 girls team to advance to the state final four was Greene, which edged Tully, 2-1, in overtime in a Class C quarterfinal Saturday behind two goals from Miah Cragle. Maine-Endwell lost to Section 5's Pittsford, 5-0, in Class A. Margaretville fell to Section 10's Lisbon Central, 3-1, in Class D. Class AAA: Arlington 1, Elmira 0 Chase Harris scored the game's only goal with 29 minutes, 58 seconds remaining and the Admirals held off the Express. A strong effort from goalie Delaney Billbe helped keep Elmira within striking distance. Express head coach Zach Sarno praised her play and that of the defense, which he said was "stellar" all season. Arlington (14-1-5) is ranked third in Class AAA by the New York State Sports Writers Association. Elmira is ranked 24th. Elmira finished with an 11-6 record that included a 2-1 victory over Ithaca in the Section 4 championship game . The Express' roster is predominantly underclassmen. "You know it's always going to be a battle when you get to this level, especially when you're playing some teams that you're not familiar with," Sarno said. "I think we worked extremely hard. We left it all out here and that's all you can ask for. ... I'm just proud of the girls today. "We work hard, but we're still a growing team. Very, very young and I would say we did everything we could this year. We're going to continue to get better." Arlington will face fellow Section 1 team Albertus Magnus in a state semifinal at 10 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 14 at Dryden High School. More: Matchups and scores for the 2026 Section 4 girls soccer tournaments Class AA: Northport 3, Horseheads 1 Maddie Ribble scored the game's final goal for Horseheads with 14 minutes remaining as the Blue Raiders' season came to a close after capturing a third consecutive Section 4 title . Ava DeMarco and Caitlin Cocks scored first-half goals for the Admirals. DeMarco scored her second goal seven minutes into the second half. Northport (16-2) will play fellow Section 11 team West Islip in a state semifinal at 2:30 p.m. Nov. 14 at Dryden High School. Northport is ranked third in the state in Class AA. Horseheads finished with a 10-4-2 record. The Blue Raiders are ranked 20th in New York in Class AA. item.title: Bexley edges Fairfield Union in regional soccer championship game
item.description: HEATH — The Fairfield Union girls’ soccer team started their Division III regional championship with a bang when senior Maddi Mitchell scored a goal on an assist from Makayla Rawlins in the first minute of the game against Bexley to give the Falcons a quick lead. However, it didn’t last, as the Lions were able to counter with a pair of goals and held on for a hard-fought 2-1 victory to end the Falcons’ season on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Heath High School. More: Fairfield Union girls soccer wins regional semifinal vs Tri-Valley Fairfield Union was making only its second-ever appearance in an Elite Eight game. It was a tough way to end the season, but Fairfield Union has nothing to be ashamed of. The Falcons finish with a 15-5-2 record, placing second (5-1) in the Mid-State League-Buckeye Division. The Falcons reached the regional final by beating Hillsboro 8-0 and Sheridan 3-1, before upsetting top-ranked Marietta 1-0 in the Southeast district championship. It marked the fourth time in the last four years that the Falcons have won a district title. From there, Fairfield Union defeated Tri-Valley 2-0 in the regional semifinal at Logan. Senior Kyla Gasser finished her outstanding career with several records. She scored her 78 th career goal in the win against Tri-Valley, which ties the school record held by Taylor Davis. item.title: Real Salt Lake clinch Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs spot
item.description: Real Salt Lake clinch Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs spot By MLSsoccer staff Real Salt Lake have qualified for the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs, clinching their spot with a 2-1 win over the LA Galaxy on Decision Day. RSL finished ninth in the Western Conference standings (45 points; 13W-15L-6D). They will visit No. 8-seeded Seattle Sounders FC in the Wild Card match. The Claret-and-Cobalt are headed to the postseason for a sixth consecutive season, including every year since head coach Pablo Mastroeni took charge in 2021. The club won MLS Cup presented by Audi in 2009 and lost in the 2013 final. Star players USMNT midfielder Diego Luna was limited by injuries this year, recording 5g/6a before undergoing season-ending knee surgery in mid-September. Despite losing Luna and transferring homegrown winger Zavier Gozo to English Premier League side Crystal Palace, RSL found form late to qualify for the postseason. Rookie striker Sergi Solans took the league by storm with 15g/4a, earning a contract extension in August. Morgan Guilavogui joined as a Designated Player from Ligue 1 side RC Lens and co-leads the team with 10 assists. Meanwhile, 2026 FIFA World Cup defenders Juan Manuel Sanabria (Uruguay) and Luc de Fougerolles (Canada) provide added quality in front of veteran goalkeeper Rafael Cabral . Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs MLS Cup presented by Audi will be played Dec. 18, while the playoffs begin Nov. 19 with Wild Card matches.
